Too many AI chats to find the good ones again? ChatNest is a side-panel organizer for AI chat folders and a prompt library. It works on ChatGPT and other popular AI chat sites. When a conversation is worth keeping, save it to a folder in one click and add a note in your own words. Later, search your saved chats by title or note and pick up where you left off. Save the prompts you reuse as templates, fill in {{variables}}, preview the result and insert it into the chat box. Your draft stays put, and ChatNest never sends a message for you. results.title: How to Organize ChatGPT Conversations: Complete Guide (2026)
results.content:
AI Toolbox (formerly ChatGPT Toolbox) is the Chrome extension built for exactly this pain: hundreds of conversations becoming unmanageable in the native ChatGPT sidebar, with no folders, no filters on its search, and no way to bulk archive a selected set of completed chats. It adds folders and subfolders, full-text search by message content, bulk export on Premium (TXT, Markdown, JSON, PDF, ZIP; the free plan exports one chat at a time as TXT), a prompt library with the `//` shortcut and `{{variable}}` placeholders, message-level bookmarks, and cross-device sync. Works on all Chromium browsers (Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, Arc, Vivaldi). Folders, search and cross-device sync all work on the permanently free plan, with usage caps on the free tier. Premium lifts those caps and adds [...] Native ChatGPT is not a blank slate for organization, so it is wrong to say it has none. It includes an archive for hiding individual conversations, the newer Projects feature for grouping related chats, files, and custom instructions under one objective, and a Library that auto-collects files from your chats. OpenAI documents how Projects work in its Projects in ChatGPT help article. What native ChatGPT does not do is offer nested folders for arbitrary conversations, search filters, or bulk organization actions on a chosen set of chats: apart from archiving every chat at once in Settings, archive runs one conversation at a time, and a Project is a flat grouping rather than a folder tree you can move chats between in bulk. That gap, nested folders for any conversation plus bulk moves, is [...] ### Create Template Conversations for Recurring Work

A template conversation is a saved chat with a proven prompt structure that you copy and reuse for new projects. Store these in a dedicated "Templates" folder and duplicate them at the start of each new instance of the task.

Examples of templates that save significant time: client onboarding questionnaires, weekly report generators, code review checklists, content outline builders, and research summary templates. AI Toolbox's prompt library feature takes this further by letting you save individual prompts and inject them into any conversation with a single click.
